summary: Reproduced the DSpark verify-position overflow in the prepared checkout and added a per-request context/generation clamp. Clipped requests use a compact ragged target layout, while unused fixed-width draft rows repeat the final legal position.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: collection failed because clamp_verify_lens was absent from the prepared source.

39 tests and 18 subtests passed, covering the reported boundary, mixed per-request context/generation budgets, an exhausted-request guard, padded draft positions, selection of the model context rather than the larger allocation width, existing DSpark scheduling, and ragged layout behavior.
On AMD MI350X gfx950, GPU tensors produced verify lengths [6, 2, 1, 2] and a maximum padded position of 1,048,575 for a 1,048,576-token context, matching an independent literal reference.
The actual GPU ragged-layout builder produced verify_lens [6, 2, 1, 2], extend_start_loc [0, 6, 8, 9], and qo_indptr [0, 6, 8, 9, 11].
The new registered test satisfies repository test-registration validation.

tests.command: pre-commit run ruff --files <changed Python files> && pre-commit run ruff-format --files <changed Python files>
tests.what_was_measured: Lint and formatting passed for all changed Python files.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-6cbc28ce321f/raw/gpu_boundary_check.txt and gpu_ragged_layout_check.txt record successful execution on AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-.
remaining_limitations: The reported two-GPU NVIDIA B300 TP2/CUDA serving workload was not reproduced on the assigned single AMD gfx950 GPU.
GPU validation covers the boundary tensor arithmetic and ragged-layout kernel, not full-model semantic accuracy or distributed execution.
